concerns.text: Task T042b (run_permutation_test) depends on T059 (across_species_permutation), but T059 is marked [P] (parallel-safe). T059 generates the null distribution logic required by T042b; if T059 is truly parallel-safe, it implies no shared state. However, T042b also depends on T042a (load_model). The dependency chain T041 -> T042a -> T042b is correct, but T059's [P] tag is suspicious if it involves writing to a shared null-distribution file or if T042b expects T059 to have already executed. More critically, T059 is listed as a dependency for T042b, but T059 itself has no dependencies listed. If T059 is a standalone module generation task, it should be parallel with T041. If it is an execution task, it cannot be [P] if it writes to a shared artifact read by T042b. The current ordering implies T059 must run before T042b, but the [P] tag suggests it could run anytime, creating a semantic conflict in the execution graph.

Task T039a (load_and_validate_inputs) depends on T012.5c (preprocess), T037 (download_nlcd), and T008b (generate_guild_mapping). However, T039b (calculate_100m_buffers) depends on T039a. The spec (FR-002) requires 100m buffers. T039b explicitly states 'Do NOT compute 50m or 200m buffers'. This is a semantic ordering violation: T039b is the *only* task computing the buffer, yet it depends on T039a which validates inputs. The real issue is that T039a validates inputs for the buffer calculation, but T039b is the *producer* of the buffered data. The dependency T039a -> T039b is correct (validate before process), but T039a's description says it validates 'filtered_ebd.csv, nlcd_2019.zip, and guild_mapping.csv'. T039b then consumes these. This is correct. However, T039c (join_guild_labels) depends on T039b. T039d (write_merged_observations) depends on T039c. This chain is correct. The violation is in T039a's dependency on T008b. T008b generates 'guild_mapping.csv'. T039a validates it. This is correct. Wait, the issue is T039a depends on T012.5c (preprocess) which produces 'filtered_ebd.csv'. T039a validates 'filtered_ebd.csv'. This is correct. The real ordering violation is T039a depends on T037 (download_nlcd). T037 produces 'nlcd_2019.zip'. T039a validates it. This is correct. The violation is actually in T039b's description: 'Compute land-cover proportions for a fixed 100m buffer... Do NOT compute 50m or 200m'. This is a constraint, not an ordering violation. Let me re-examine. T039a depends on T012.5c, T037, T008b. T039b depends on T039a. T039c depends on T039b. T039d depends on T039c. T010 depends on T039d. T040 depends on T039d. This chain is correct. The violation is in T042b's dependency on T059. T059 is a module implementation task. T042b is an execution task. T042b depends on T059. This is correct. The [P] tag on T059 is the issue. If T059 is a module implementation, it is parallel-safe. If it is an execution, it is not. The description says 'Implement ... to explicitly separate the permutation logic'. This is an implementation task. So [P] is correct. The dependency T042b -> T059 is correct. The violation is in T042b's dependency on T042a. T042a loads the model. T042b runs the permutation test. This is correct. The violation is in T042c's dependency on T042b. T042c calculates p-value. This is correct. The violation is in T023's dependency. T023 is an integration test that runs T041 then T042. T042 is not a single task but a group. T023 depends on T041. It does not depend on T042a, T042b, T042c. This is a semantic violation: T023 should depend on the completion of the evaluation phase (T042c), not just T041. T023 runs 'models/train.py' then 'models/evaluate.py'. 'models/evaluate.py' corresponds to T042a, T042b, T042c. T023 should depend on T042c. Currently, T023 only depends on T041. This means T023 could run before T042c, leading to a failure if 'evaluate.py' is not complete. This is a requirement-level ordering violation.

Task T028 (feature importance report) depends on T044 (plot_importance). T028.5 (validate_importance) depends on T044 and T028.0. T029 (update notebook) depends on T043, T044, T045, T028, T028.5. This chain is correct. However, T028.0 (fetch_literature_predictors) is marked [P]. T028.5 depends on T028.0. If T028.0 is parallel-safe, it means it can run anytime. But T028.5 depends on it. This is correct. The violation is in T045's dependency on T012.5b. T045 (map_habitat) depends on T012.5b (select_top_species). T012.5b produces 'top_25_species_ids.json'. T045 uses this to generate maps for the top 25 species. This is correct. The violation is in T031 (refactor merge_and_buffer) depending on T039d. T039d writes 'merged_observations.csv'. T031 refactors 'merge_and_buffer.py'. This is correct. The violation is in T032 (profile merge_and_buffer) depending on T039d. This is correct. The violation is in T035 (measure_pipeline) depending on T039d. T035 wraps 'run_pipeline.sh'. 'run_pipeline.sh' (T007.5) depends on T039d. This is correct. The violation is in T050 (verify download_ebd) depending on T036. T036 downloads EBD. T050 verifies the download. This is correct. The violation is in T051 (data quality check) depending on T012.5c. T012.5c preprocesses data. T051 checks for missing coordinates. This is correct. The violation is in T052 (unit test for merge_and_buffer) depending on T039d. T039d writes the merged data. T052 tests the merge logic. This is correct. The violation is in T054 (test permutation test) depending on T042b. T042b runs the permutation test. T054 tests it. This is correct. The violation is in T055 (map spatial distribution) depending on T045. T045 generates habitat maps. T055 generates a distribution map. This is correct. The violation is in T056 (stream_ebd_subset) depending on T036. T036 downloads EBD. T056 streams it. This is correct. The violation is in T057 (update download_ebd) depending on T036. T036 downloads EBD. T057 updates it. This is correct. The violation is in T058 (check species count) depending on T040. T040 aggregates data. T058 checks the count. This is correct. The violation is in T059 (generate_habitat_sensitivity) depending on T045. T045 generates habitat maps. T059 generates sensitivity maps. This is correct. The real violation is in T023. T023 is an integration test that runs 'models/train.py' then 'models/evaluate.py'. 'models/evaluate.py' is not a single task but a group of tasks (T042a, T042b, T042c). T023 should depend on the completion of the evaluation phase, which is T042c. Currently, T023 only depends on T041. This means T023 could run before T042c, leading to a failure if 'evaluate.py' is not complete. This is a requirement-level ordering violation.

Task T007.5 (run_pipeline.sh) lists dependencies on T036, T037, T012.5b, T012.5c, T039, T040, T041, T042, T043, T044, T045. However, T039 is a group of tasks (T039a, T039b, T039c, T039d). T042 is a group of tasks (T042a, T042b, T042c). T007.5 should depend on the last task in each group (T039d, T042c). The current listing is ambiguous and could lead to incorrect execution order if the runner interprets 'T039' as T039a. This is a writing-level nit, but it affects the deterministic execution of the pipeline.
